paragraphs.source_en: Yet from the very outset of the battle, a flaw appeared in the plan. The Echizen army charged forward recklessly, and Honda Tadatomo, unwilling to be outdone, launched an attack as well. Then the Ogasawara army also swept into the fray, leaving Mōri Katsunaga no choice but to meet them in battle.

paragraphs.source_en: To rouse his men's spirits, he had declared with fervor, “Today we shall stake our lives and fight with our backs to the wall!” Even so, he had not forgotten what the battle was being fought for. Every battle held countless chances for the tide to turn; victory or defeat was never absolute.

paragraphs.source_en: Mōri Katsunaga, however, did not grasp Yukimura's intentions so deeply. That was the difference between the two men. Resolved to die rather than live in dishonor, Mōri Katsunaga thought that death awaited them in any case, so they might as well fight to the finish. The difference in their thinking ultimately kept Yukimura from halting Mōri's advance and greatly diminished the original plan.

paragraphs.source_en: Victory in the opening clash was no true victory! To accept battle rashly was to risk being drawn into the enemy ranks... For Yukimura, this was a crushing blow. His vision darkened, and he was powerless to stop Mōri's blood-crazed troops as they raced across the battlefield like unbridled horses.

paragraphs.source_en: Yukimura had sought to capture the king by first taking the bandits' chief, but he had not reckoned on the Ii and Tōdō forces rushing so desperately to the rescue. paragraphs.source_en: The distance between Chausuyama and Ieyasu's great formation grew ever shorter, leaving Yukimura almost no room to maneuver. He himself had changed horses twice and was drenched in blood. Now, just as he was about to lead his men in another retreat, he saw the banners of the Echizen army already fluttering before his own position.

units.source_en: He himself had changed horses twice and was drenched in blood.
units.source_zh: 他本人也曾两次更换战马，浑身是血。

units.source_en: Now, just as he was about to lead his men in another retreat, he saw the banners of the Echizen army already fluttering before his own position.
units.source_zh: 此时，他正欲再次率人撤退，却发现越前军的旗帜已飘至自己阵前。

paragraphs.source_zh: 茶磨山和家康大阵之间的距离越来越短，几无可让幸村左右腾挪的余地。他虽强撑发动了三次进攻，杀入敌阵三五次，可叹人马俱疲，多是有去无回。他本人也曾两次更换战马，浑身是血。此时，他正欲再次率人撤退，却发现越前军的旗帜已飘至自己阵前。

paragraphs.source_en: Matsudaira Tadanao was the first to fight his way onto Chausuyama.

units.source_en: Matsudaira Tadanao was the first to fight his way onto Chausuyama.
units.source_zh: 松平忠直率先杀上了茶磨山。

paragraphs.source_zh: 松平忠直率先杀上了茶磨山。

paragraphs.source_en: Yukimura looked up to heaven and gave a long sigh. Such had been his loyalty and courage, such his strategy, and such the battle—was this the will of heaven?

units.source_en: Yukimura looked up to heaven and gave a long sigh. Such had been his loyalty and courage, such his strategy, and such the battle—was this the will of heaven?
units.source_zh: 幸村仰天长叹一声，忠勇如是，谋略如是，战已如是，此天意乎？

paragraphs.source_zh: 幸村仰天长叹一声，忠勇如是，谋略如是，战已如是，此天意乎？

paragraphs.source_en: Yukimura had lost all desire to fight again. Thus ended his final battle with Tokugawa Ieyasu, who had ridden the fields of war for sixty years. He could not help sighing again: beneath all heaven, who understood his heart?

units.source_en: Yukimura had lost all desire to fight again. Thus ended his final battle with Tokugawa Ieyasu, who had ridden the fields of war for sixty years.
units.source_zh: 幸村已了无再战之意，他和驰骋疆场六十载的德川家康的最后一战，就这样结束了。

units.source_en: He could not help sighing again: beneath all heaven, who understood his heart?

ja.t: かずにはいられなかった。この

units.source_zh: 他不由再叹，普天之下，谁识我心？

paragraphs.source_zh: 幸村已了无再战之意，他和驰骋疆场六十载的德川家康的最后一战，就这样结束了。他不由再叹，普天之下，谁识我心？

paragraphs.source_en: He rode to Yasui Tenjin Shrine and dismounted in its small courtyard. By then his whole body was wounded and his limbs were powerless; he could barely remain standing.

units.source_en: He rode to Yasui Tenjin Shrine and dismounted in its small courtyard.
units.source_zh: 他打马来到安居天神神社，在小院里下了马。

units.source_en: By then his whole body was wounded and his limbs were powerless; he could barely remain standing.

ja.t: っていることさえおぼつかなかった。

units.source_zh: 此时他已浑身是伤，四肢无力，几站立不稳。

paragraphs.source_zh: 他打马来到安居天神神社，在小院里下了马。此时他已浑身是伤，四肢无力，几站立不稳。

paragraphs.source_en: Yukimura went beneath an ever-burning lantern and, swaying, was about to bend down and sit when a man behind him shouted, “I am Nishio Nizaemon, a warrior of Echizen! Who are you?”

units.source_en: Yukimura went beneath an ever-burning lantern and, swaying, was about to bend down and sit when a man behind him shouted, “I am Nishio Nizaemon, a warrior of Echizen! Who are you?”

ja.t: ろそうとした。そのとき

units.source_zh: 幸村走到一盏长明灯下，摇晃着正欲弯腰坐下，只听身后有人高喊：“我乃越前武士西尾仁左卫门，尔乃何人？”

paragraphs.source_zh: 幸村走到一盏长明灯下，摇晃着正欲弯腰坐下，只听身后有人高喊：“我乃越前武士西尾仁左卫门，尔乃何人？”

paragraphs.source_en: Yukimura tried to rise and give his name, but his body would not obey him. Before he could struggle to his feet, an iron blade was thrust into his belly. A surge of agony swept through him, and he could no longer speak.

units.source_en: Yukimura tried to rise and give his name, but his body would not obey him.

ja.t: うことをきかなかった。

units.source_zh: 幸村试图站起来，报上名姓，身体却不听使唤。

units.source_en: Before he could struggle to his feet, an iron blade was thrust into his belly.
units.source_zh: 他挣扎着还未站起，便被一把铁刃刺入了腹部。

units.source_en: A surge of agony swept through him, and he could no longer speak.

ja.t: することもできなかった。

units.source_zh: 他感到一阵剧痛，更说不出话。

paragraphs.source_zh: 幸村试图站起来，报上名姓，身体却不听使唤。他挣扎着还未站起，便被一把铁刃刺入了腹部。他感到一阵剧痛，更说不出话。

paragraphs.source_en: So this was death? Ah, compared with life, death was indeed simple and dull.

units.source_en: So this was death?
units.source_zh: 这便是死亡吗？

units.source_en: Ah, compared with life, death was indeed simple and dull.
units.source_zh: 哦，这死，与生相比，确是简单而无趣。

paragraphs.source_zh: 这便是死亡吗？哦，这死，与生相比，确是简单而无趣。

paragraphs.source_en: Nishio Nizaemon thrust once with his spear, then kicked the fallen man. Seeing no response, he drew his sword and cut off Yukimura's head.

units.source_en: Nishio Nizaemon thrust once with his spear, then kicked the fallen man. Seeing no response, he drew his sword and cut off Yukimura's head.
units.source_zh: 西尾仁左卫门刺了一枪，又踢一脚，见倒地之人已无任何反应，便一刀砍下了幸村头颅。
